qualifier_repro_before_fix.volatile_header: typedef volatile unsigned T; struct S { T bits:3; };
qualifier_repro_before_fix.c_source:
#include "struct_volatile.h"
unsigned twice(const struct S *p) { return p->bits + p->bits; }
qualifier_repro_before_fix.const_note: GCC diagnoses the read-only assignment as a warning without -Werror; Clang rejects it. Both fail with the recorded -Werror commands. Generated Rust accepted and executed the setter before the fix.

coverage: Six direct, typedef-qualified, and unnamed volatile bitfield declarations are rejected across structs and unions.
Const direct and typedef-qualified getters compile; ordinary mutable setters compile and execute for structs and unions.
Four const setters fail Rust compilation with E0599; corresponding C assignments fail GCC and Clang with readonly diagnostics.
Existing native union byte/callback tests, five-target Clang layouts, and aggregate/struct bitfield FFI regressions pass.
fixed_validation.scope: Native C/Rust execution on x86_64 Linux only; cross-target tests check Clang layouts and do not execute foreign target code.

positive_scenarios: struct byte gaps remain uninitialized MaybeUninit padding
miri.negative_scenario: intentionally uninitialized overlapping byte; unsafe accessor contract violated
miri.negative_diagnostic: Undefined Behavior: reading memory ... memory is uninitialized

reproducer.c_union_header: union U { unsigned bit:1; unsigned bytes[4]; };
reproducer.c_struct_header: struct S { unsigned a:1; unsigned :23; unsigned b:1; };
